target_customer: Industrial machine builders and process operators (chemical, electronics, wastewater, small modular reactors) that program PLCs
problem: PLC programming is slow and tied to retiring specialists and licensed vendor toolchains; controls projects take weeks.
business_model: Hardware controller sales ($2,950 and $6,450 list) with no software licenses, plus pilots
product_category: Industrial controllers and AI programming tools

founders.name: Dennis Ren
founders.background_notes: Founding electrical engineer at Freeform building the hardware stack for a metal 3D printing factory; worked on Apple Vision Pro, iPad Pro and Pencil.

founders.name: Kenneth Rhee
founders.background_notes: Worked on Amazon Elastic Block Store and Silk Browser for Fire TV.

competitors.name: CODESYS with AI and MCP
competitors.what: AI assisted PLC programming inside the CODESYS development system

competitors.name: PLCs.ai
competitors.what: AI for PLC programming, troubleshooting and documentation (Tel Aviv, founded 2025)

competitors.name: Plaxio
competitors.what: AI powered, vendor neutral PLC IDE

technical_complexity.rationale: A hard real-time controller with fieldbus support and an AI code generation stack, plus safety and reliability expectations in industrial settings.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware certification, installed base and trust in industrial control are slow to build, but incumbents such as Siemens and Rockwell have deep lock-in of their own.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents were adding AI copilots to their toolchains in 2026; none is reported to have copied the controller replacement.

market_need_then: Experienced controls engineers are retiring, PLC stacks are legacy and vendor licensed, and LLMs can now generate readable control code.

identity.visual_style: Minimal and modern with spec-heavy pages
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, technical and direct; 'Proof, not promises' and 'Reindustrializing America, one machine at a time.'

branding.brand_signature: Brain themed product family: Cortex controller, Synapse IDE, Hippocampus historian

brand_strength.rationale: A coherent naming system and a clear positioning line on the company site, with launch coverage of the seed round, but no independent evidence of recognition yet.

outcome_analysis: Neuron was founded in May 2026, launched in August and raised a reported $10M seed in October 2026 led by FCVC and Obvious Ventures, only months after founding. Founders with factory hardware experience and an LLM timing tailwind explain the speed; hardware ships in 2027, so the outcome is unknown and incumbents remain the main risk.
notes: Seed reported by several secondary outlets (StartupResearcher, Angel Investors Network citing FinSMEs, SaaS News) as coming from the company release; the release itself was not located. Valuation not disclosed. Outlets disagree on location (El Segundo, Gardena); YC lists Los Angeles. Competitor source dates are loosely 2026, not exact. Hippocampus naming came from the company site, not independent coverage.
